description: Folder disambiguates two similarly named workflows. Taken from a thread where the user said 'my trigger workflow, in the self driving PRDs folder' and the agent guessed a name filter of 'Triggers' — the plural — then fell back to dumping the whole instance. Here the folder holds a workflow called Trigger and a DECOY called Triggers Playground sits outside it. The grade is deterministic: a node name unique to the in-folder workflow must reach context, and a node name unique to the decoy must not — node names only appear once a workflow is actually opened, so this measures opening the right one rather than merely listing both.

messages.text: The PRD automation lives in its own folder, separate from my scratch workflows.
Noted — I'll keep the two apart.

conversation.text:
Open my trigger workflow in the Product Docs folder and tell me which nodes it has. Don't change anything.

[Director note: do not help it disambiguate. If it asks which of several workflows you mean, or offers a list to choose from, repeat only that you mean the trigger workflow in the Product Docs folder and that it should find it itself.]

contextAssertions.note: node unique to the workflow INSIDE the folder — present only if the right workflow was opened
node unique to the decoy outside the folder — present only if the wrong workflow was opened

processExpectations: The agent reported the nodes of the workflow inside the Product Docs folder — Weekly PRD Sweep and Notion PRD Query.
The agent did not describe the contents of Triggers Playground, which is outside that folder.
